title: Humane AI Pin: The $699 Hardware Collapse
subtitle: When Daily Returns Surpassed New Sales
description: A venture-backed hardware failure where telecom IMEI constraints turned returns into unrefurbishable e-waste, driving negative sales velocity until HP acquired the software and bricked the hardware.

beats.title: Sales & Returns Inversion
beats.narration: For three months, more people returned the AI Pin than bought one.

beats.title: Launch & Negative Velocity
beats.narration: Humane pitched a $699 lapel pin designed to replace the smartphone. They shipped about 10,000 units, pulling in roughly $9 million. Then net sales went negative. Between May and August 2024, daily returns consistently surpassed new orders.

beats.title: Carrier Locking & E-Waste Trap
beats.narration: Over $1 million in hardware bounced back to their warehouse. Worse, Humane couldn't even resell the returned devices. Because of T-Mobile carrier locking constraints, they couldn't wipe and reassign the internal cellular chips. Thousands of returned pins turned directly into e-waste.

beats.title: Asset Sale & Hardware Abandonment
beats.narration: By August, active users dropped below 7,000. And in February 2025, HP bought Humane's software assets for $116 million, ditching the hardware entirely.

beats.title: Cloud Shutdown & Bricked Hardware
beats.narration: On February 28, the cloud servers shut down. Every pin, bricked instantly. That's $699 for a silent metal badge.
